projects.title: SRMD Multilingual Speech Translation
projects.summary: A multilingual speech-translation pipeline for Gujarati spiritual discourse, from dataset preparation through evaluation.
projects.role: Contributed to dataset preparation, evaluation-metric design, and Gujarati-to-English training.
projects.problem: Gujarati spiritual discourse needed to reach a global audience, which means speech recognition, alignment and translation that hold up on domain-specific vocabulary in a low-resource language.
built: Dataset preparation and evaluation-metric design for the pipeline.
projects.approach: The pipeline combines speech recognition, alignment and translation components built around Whisper and NVIDIA NeMo.
projects.evaluation: An evaluation loop combining synthetic examples, human review, baseline comparisons, and an LLM judge that flagged domain-vocabulary errors for review and retraining.
projects.result: The broader product supports eight languages and has reached 1.2M+ users across 190+ countries. This is product-wide reach, not attributable to my work alone.

projects.title: Wisdom Multimodal Search and RAG
projects.summary: Search across webpages, articles, audio, video, and PDFs, including timestamped video results.

stat.label: median end-to-end latency at 10,000+ monthly users

projects.role: Built the multimodal search and retrieval system.
projects.problem: Users needed one search experience across very different content types, including jumping to the right moment inside a video.
built: Search across webpages, articles, audio, video, and PDFs.
projects.approach: Hybrid retrieval using Voyage embeddings, Weaviate and BM25, with an in-house timestamping model and an LLM reranking stage.
projects.result: Production search serving 10,000+ monthly users with sub-1.5-second median end-to-end latency and a 93% click-through rate.

projects.title: Prompt Invariant Training (PIT)
projects.summary: Robustness of LLM mathematical reasoning to plausible but irrelevant prompt context.
projects.problem: LLMs can lose a correct answer when a prompt includes plausible but irrelevant context. The question is whether training can make reasoning invariant to it.
built: Generated distracting context without changing the underlying question, then checked whether the original answer remained valid.
projects.approach: Compared standard SFT, Noise-CoT SFT, and latent-aligned fine-tuning on a Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B model family.
projects.result: Adversarial reasoning accuracy rose from 21.57% (baseline) to 41.1% with Noise-CoT SFT and 48.3% with latent-aligned fine-tuning, with a slight clean-prompt accuracy trade-off.

projects.title: Physics-Inspired Crowd-Risk Detection
projects.summary: A fluid-mechanics-inspired risk score for spotting regions of video where dangerous crowd conditions may be developing.

stat.label: optical-flow endpoint error after fine-tuning RAFT

projects.problem: Spotting a crowd that is becoming dangerous depends on how people are moving, not just how many there are.
built: A crowd-risk score combining density, motion, optical flow, and directional variation.
Fine-tuned RAFT optical flow on CrowdFlow.
projects.approach: Borrows ideas from fluid mechanics to turn per-region density and flow fields into a single risk signal.
projects.result: Reduced endpoint error from 1.110 to 0.5644 on held-out evaluation data.

projects.title: LLM-Assisted CUDA Kernel Performance Prediction
projects.summary: A hybrid approach to predicting CUDA kernel runtime from code and hardware characteristics.

stat.label: on 100 CUDA kernels, 20% better than baseline

projects.problem: Estimating how long a GPU kernel will run, without profiling it on every target, is useful for performance work.
built: A hybrid runtime-prediction approach combining static CUDA code characteristics, LLM-derived code semantics, and GPU hardware characteristics.
projects.evaluation: Evaluated on 100 CUDA kernels run on the NYU cluster.
projects.result: 5% MAPE, a 20% improvement over the baseline.

projects.title: Drone Obstacle Avoidance with Selective VLM Reasoning
projects.summary: A simulated pipeline that escalates only uncertain cases to a vision-language model.

stat.label: lower latency than baseline at 95% pipeline accuracy

projects.problem: Difficult obstacles such as wires and glass call for deeper reasoning, but running a large model on every frame is costly.
built: A simulated obstacle-avoidance pipeline with a fast perception stage and a risk gate.
projects.approach: The risk gate escalates uncertain cases to Qwen, which reasons about difficult obstacles such as wires and glass.
projects.result: 95% end-to-end pipeline accuracy and 45% lower latency than the baseline on the same workload.

projects.title: Face Recognition for Community Deployments
projects.summary: An open-source Siamese face-recognition model trained on Indian faces and deployed for community use.
projects.role: Built the model and mentored contributors through GirlScript Summer of Code.
projects.problem: A community deployment needed face recognition that works well on Indian faces.
built: A Siamese face-recognition model with ResNet-based embeddings and triplet loss.
Augmentation and a dataset of Indian faces.
Open-sourced the implementation and mentored contributors through GirlScript Summer of Code.
projects.result: The deployment site had a membership base exceeding 8,000.

experiences.title: Data Analytics Intern
bullets: Built a hybrid NLP pipeline that classifies insurance claims as occurring during construction or after completion: claim-description embeddings with logistic regression, plus a prompt-tuned Gemma 4 fallback for low-confidence or conflicting predictions. On 11,000 records it reached 99% accuracy and ~89% PR-AUC.

Built an unsupervised claims-analysis workflow with embeddings and HDBSCAN, followed by manual review of noise clusters and threshold tuning, enabling claim-category loss-ratio analysis across MGAs rather than aggregate-level analysis alone.
Trained a Random Forest model to predict one-year loan delinquency from monthly loan data using a time-based split, reaching 91% accuracy.

experiences.title: Co-Founder and Founding Engineer
bullets: Building open-source behavioral testing and evaluation infrastructure for LLM and agentic applications, initially focused on AI risk assessment and insurability.

Built a Python SDK with callback-based instrumentation that captures application traces with minimal changes to existing application logic, and a dashboard that connects traces, test cases, expected outputs and current outputs to surface behavioral drift and regressions across model, prompt and configuration changes.
Implemented golden tests, custom tests, repeatable evaluations, and persona-driven simulations covering more than ten attack and failure scenarios.
Supported five active users across organizations and folded their framework-compatibility feedback into the SDK.

experiences.title: Machine Learning Engineer
bullets: Built an automated red-teaming framework for AI chatbots covering adversarial prompt generation, execution and scoring against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, using Llama 3.1 and Phi-3.5 Mini.
Created a five-point severity-grading workflow with human-reviewed ground truth, reducing assessment effort from roughly eight hours of manual testing to under five hours of reviewer time.

Built a website security-scoring pipeline using a locally deployed Gemma 3 27B model to screen webpage text and screenshots for potential exposure of user information, including healthcare privacy concerns. Scanned 10,000+ domains and generated concise reports for CISO review.

experiences.title: Machine Learning Engineer
bullets: Built a multimodal music recommendation workflow combining facial embeddings, speech-derived features and text sentiment, with a meta-audio model generating an audio tone aligned with each recommendation. Manual evaluation by 50 users yielded 84% recommendation quality, and latency fell 40% relative to the prior implementation.

Developed a handwritten-document OCR pipeline evaluated across 100,000+ documents with 87% extraction accuracy, using augmentation and region-specific labels to improve tickmark localization and category mapping.

about: I'm an MS Computer Science student at NYU Courant, working on reliable AI systems: how to test LLM applications, retrieve across messy multimodal content, and make vision and GPU workloads faster and more trustworthy.

Before NYU I worked as an ML engineer at Blueinfy and NightHack, building red-teaming and security-screening tools and multimodal pipelines. Now I'm co-founding LitmusAI, open-source evaluation infrastructure for LLM and agentic apps.
I'm most motivated by technology that is accessible and socially useful, from multilingual speech translation to face recognition built for local communities.
